title: Function-calling observability & graceful-fallback playbook
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Define acceptance criteria and operational runbook for function-calling integrations that balance developer ergonomics, deterministic retries, and observability for partial/streamed structured outputs.
background: Customers are integrating Redwood function-calling to reach external tool adapters and internal action runners. We’ve observed intermittent schema mismatches, partial stream failures, and opaque retry behavior that cause production errors and poor DX.
This ticket captures acceptance criteria for behavior, telemetry, and a rollout playbook so engineering can implement consistent fallbacks and SRE can operate predictable remediation steps.
problem_statement: Unclear semantics when a streamed structured response contains malformed frames: callers don't know whether to retry, fall back to non-stream mode, or surface partial results.
Tool adapters (third-party and internal) have divergent retry semantics leading to duplicate side-effects or lost events.
Lack of standardized telemetry for function-call success/failure categories impedes root-cause and SLA calculation.
goals: Specify deterministic success/failure semantics for function-calls across sync and streaming paths.
Define telemetry events and labels needed to monitor quality and guide automated rollbacks.
Ship a minimal operator playbook (canary/kill-switch/metrics) and acceptance tests that verify graceful degradation modes.
non_goals: Changing underlying adapter SDKs for third-party tools (this ticket focuses on platform behavior and surface contracts).
Comprehensive migration for all legacy customers in the initial rollout; we'll provide opt-in toggles and communication templates instead.
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-visible function-call errors (schema mismatch and stream-frame failures) by 60% in first 30 days post-rollout.
>= 95% of function-calls labeled with full telemetry (connector, adapter-version, call-path, response-mode) within 2 days of deployment.
No production incidents caused by duplicate side-effects from automated retries during the canary phase.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Deterministic final-state semantics documented: for each failure class (schema_violation, adapter_reject, transient_network, partial_stream_end, unrecoverable_error) the platform returns a documented status code and resolution recommendation (retry, idempotent-retry, fail-fast, partial-commit).

AC-2: Streaming frame protocol includes a monotonically increasing frame_id and optional checkpoint_token every N frames (configurable); consumers can safely resume when provided a checkpoint_token or receive a clear terminal frame when stream is complete.

AC-3: Implement a 'function-bridge' adapter contract: adapters must acknowledge invocation with a 2xx ack-with-id or a 4xx/5xx failure payload. Platform retries only if ack indicates retryable; idempotency-key behavior must be respected by adapters.

AC-4: On schema mismatch inside a streaming response, platform must emit a 'stream_schema_violation' event, surface a human-readable error in the final response, and atomically provide last-consistent-checkpoint_token for best-effort resume. Calling client receives an explicit field 'partial_result': true or false.

AC-5: Telemetry emitted per function-call: call_id, adapter_name, adapter_version, mode (sync|stream), frame_count, checkpoint_count, final_status (ok|partial|failed), failure_class, latency_p50/p95, tokens_emitted. All events conform to the platform telemetry schema and are exported to Datadog and internal SLIs dashboards.

AC-6: Backpressure/backoff contract for streaming adapters: adapters may send 'X-Adapter-Backpressure' header with suggested window_ms; platform honors suggestion up to configured max and records backpressure events in telemetry.

AC-7: Automated rollback signal defined: if rollout canary breaches either (a) error rate > 3% over 5m for critical customers or (b) partial_result rate > 10% over 1h, rollout is automatically halted and traffic routed to previous stable model/adapter variant.

AC-8: End-to-end integration tests covering: successful streaming call, early schema violation, adapter transient failures with idempotent retry, duplicate-suppression behavior, and resume-from-checkpoint flows. Tests runnable in CI with mocked adapter endpoints.
implementation_notes: Platform will add explicit response envelope fields: __call_id, __frame_id, __checkpoint_token, __partial_result (bool), __failure_code. These are reserved and must not collide with user schema keys.
Add lightweight adapter-side SDK helpers (reference implementations in Go and Python) that implement ack/retry/idempotency semantics; make them example artifacts, not gating the contract.
Runtime: ensure low-overhead prefix caching still opaque to envelope fields; extended metadata stored in request-level tracing tags, not in token stream payload.
telemetry_requirements: Counter: function.call.invocations by adapter_name, mode, release (daily rollup).
Histogram: function.call.latency_ms with p50/p95/p99, split by success/failure/partial.
Event stream: function.call.schema_violation with call_id, offending_frame_id, validation_errors (stringified list), and last_checkpoint_token.
Alert: SLO breach alert when call_error_rate (final_status!=ok) > 1% for >30m for customers on Dedicated with SLA.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Integration tests and infra changes behind feature-flag in staging. Verify telemetry and CI tests (1 week).
Phase 1: Internal canary (5% of internal traffic) for 48h, validate no duplicate side-effects and monitor partial_result rate. If safe, proceed.
Phase 2: Customer canary (select customers opted in; target mix: hosted/Dedicated) for 7 days. Monitor defined metrics; enable automated rollback triggers.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with close monitoring and customer comms including SDK guide and migration notes.
risks: Adapters that do not implement idempotency will produce duplicate side-effects; mitigation: opt-in enforcement and developer guide with sample SDK code.
Telemetry volume increase may require additional retention tuning; mitigation: sample high-cardinality fields and aggregate for long-term storage.
Customer confusion around reserved envelope fields; mitigation: documentation, migration checklist, and opt-out flag for legacy integrations.
qa_steps: Run CI integration suite that mocks adapter responses: success, transient 5xx, permanent 4xx, malformed frames, and checkpoint resume. All tests must pass.
Perform manual test with internal adapter that intentionally returns a schema violation mid-stream and confirm last_checkpoint_token present and partial_result=true.
Validate that Datadog dashboards show the new telemetry and that alerting rules trigger during simulated fault injection.
